extracted.intended_audience: investigators preparing NIH grant biosketches (PIs, senior/key personnel, and other significant contributors)
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing NIH-format biographical sketches for key personnel and senior/key personnel on grant applications, following required sections, page limits, and formatting conventions. Includes education/training, personal statement, positions/honors, contributions to science, and recent research support entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall format and order
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the following information for the key personnel and other significant contributors in the order listed on Form Page 2. Follow this format for each person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeat the specified sections (name, position, education/training, A–D (Personal statement; Positions and Honors; Contributions to Science; Research projects)) for each person in the order required by Form Page 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page limit for key personnel biosketch
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The biographical sketch for key personnel and other significant contributors must be no longer than four pages when following the provided format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page limit for senior/key personnel biosketch
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the instructions specify the senior/key personnel variant, the biographical sketch for that category may be up to five pages. Follow the appropriate page-limit instruction for the category of the person.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required person-identifying fields
rubrics_metrics.description: NAME; POSITION TITLE; eRA COMMONS USER NAME (credential, e.g., agency login).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include full name, current position title, and the eRA Commons user name (agency credential) at the top of each person's biosketch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education/Training table content and order
rubrics_metrics.description: EDUCATION/TRAINING (Begin with baccalaureate or other initial professional education, such as nursing, and include postdoctoral training.) INSTITUTION AND LOCATION; DEGREE (if applicable); YEAR(s) (or Completion date MM/YYYY); FIELD OF STUDY.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List education and training starting from the earliest (baccalaureate) through postdoctoral training, including institution and location, degree (if applicable), year(s) or completion date in MM/YYYY format, and field of study. Include residency/training where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: A. Personal Statement
rubrics_metrics.description: A Personal Statement that describes current position, research focus, relevant accomplishments, and how the individual's background/experience qualifies them to contribute to the proposed project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize unique qualifications, relevant expertise, and the specific role the person will play on the proposed project. Use concise narrative examples (as shown in sample personal statements) to justify inclusion and describe anticipated contributions/oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: B. Positions and Honors
rubrics_metrics.description: List positions held and honors awarded in chronological order (employment history, visiting positions, editorial roles, society memberships, ad-hoc study section service, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include dates and institutional affiliations; highlight relevant advisory/editorial/service roles and honors that demonstrate expertise and leadership relevant to the proposed work.

rubrics_metrics.name: C. Contributions to Science
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a narrative of the individual's major contributions to science with numbered topical items and representative citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each contribution/topic, give a concise description (what was discovered/established/innovated) and list representative publications (full citations). A full bibliographic list may be provided via a URL (e.g., PubMed link). Use the sample numbered-contribution format shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representative publications and linking to full publication list
rubrics_metrics.description: Include representative peer-reviewed citations for contributions and provide a link to a full list of published work (e.g., PubMed/My NCBI bibliography).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite key papers under each contribution; if desired/available, include a URL to the full bibliography for completeness and verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: D. Research projects (ongoing and completed in past 3 years)
rubrics_metrics.description: List research projects ongoing or completed in the past 3 years with project title, grant number, funding source, project dates, role on project, percent effort, and total direct costs (where applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Format examples: grant number / PI name / dates; followed by a brief statement of the project's major goal and the individual's role (e.g., 'Role: Principal Investigator, 10% effort. Total direct costs: $'). Include completed and ongoing support with dates and effort percentages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow-the-format instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow this format for each person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The same sectional format (personal statement, positions/honors, contributions, research support) should be applied consistently to every individual listed; adapt the page-limit accordingly for the category (key vs senior/key).

rubrics_metrics.name: Begin Education/Training with earliest professional education
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin with baccalaureate or other initial professional education and include subsequent training such as postdoctoral training or residency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not omit the earliest relevant formal training; present training sequentially so reviewers can see the full training trajectory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role clarity and relevance in Personal Statement and Research Support
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly state the individual's role on the proposed project and in listed research support (e.g., consultant, PI, co-I) and contextualize why their expertise is relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Personal Statement to explain how past work and current activities position the person to perform the proposed role; in Research Support entries, provide percent effort and role to quantify contribution.
